subproblem.title: Height and L² height bounds from a net near an affine plane (Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5, (6) and conclusion)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (S : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (F : Finset (Euclid P)) (ξ x₀ : Euclid P) (r s L : ℝ), (∀ x ∈ μ.support ∩ closedBall ξ r, ∃ y ∈ F, dist x y ≤ s) → (∀ y ∈ F, ‖(y - x₀) - S.starProjection (y - x₀)‖ ≤ L) → dist x₀ ξ ≤ s → (∀ x ∈ μ.support ∩ closedBall ξ r, ‖(x - ξ) - S.starProjection (x - ξ)‖ ≤ 2 * s + L) ∧ ∫⁻ x in closedBall ξ r, ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - ξ) - S.starProjection (x - ξ)‖ ^ 2) ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * s + L) ^ 2) * μ (closedBall ξ r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the second inequality of Step 6, Step 7 and the height part of Step 8 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5 (book chapter-05.txt lines 356–374): (6), the passage via (2) from the points y_j to all of spt μ ∩ B_1(0), and the bound on ∫dist² that is combined with Remark 2.2. Here it is stated for arbitrary F, x₀, S, s and L.
Notation: q(v) := v − p_S(v) for v ∈ ℝ^P; dist(u, v) = |u − v|.

1. Properties of q. q is additive, q(u + v) = q(u) + q(v), because p_S is linear. Moreover q(v) = p_{S⊥}(v), the orthogonal projection of v onto the orthogonal complement S⊥ (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal_val). Hence |q(v)| ≤ |v| (Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le).

2. Proof of (a). Let x ∈ spt μ ∩ B̄_r(ξ), and by (i) choose y ∈ F with |x − y| = dist(x, y) ≤ s. Since x − ξ = (x − y) + (y − x₀) + (x₀ − ξ), Step 1 and the triangle inequality give
|q(x − ξ)| ≤ |q(x − y)| + |q(y − x₀)| + |q(x₀ − ξ)| ≤ |x − y| + L + |x₀ − ξ| ≤ s + L + s = 2s + L.
The middle inequality uses |q(x − y)| ≤ |x − y|, hypothesis (ii) for y, and |q(x₀ − ξ)| ≤ |x₀ − ξ| = dist(x₀, ξ) ≤ s by (iii).

3. The support has full measure. ℝ^P is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so the complement of spt μ is μ-null (Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support). Therefore μ-a.e. x, and hence μ⌞B̄_r(ξ)-a.e. x (ae_restrict_of_ae), lies in spt μ. Also μ⌞B̄_r(ξ)-a.e. x lies in the closed, hence Borel, ball B̄_r(ξ) (ae_restrict_mem).

4. Proof of (b). By Step 3, for μ⌞B̄_r(ξ)-a.e. x we have x ∈ spt μ ∩ B̄_r(ξ). For such x, (a) gives 0 ≤ |q(x − ξ)| ≤ 2s + L. Hence |q(x − ξ)|² ≤ (2s + L)², since squaring is monotone on [0, ∞), and ofReal(|q(x − ξ)|²) ≤ ofReal((2s + L)²). By monotonicity of the lower integral under a.e. inequalities (lintegral_mono_ae) and the integral of a constant over a set (setLIntegral_const),
∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} ofReal(|q(x − ξ)|²) dμ ≤ ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} ofReal((2s + L)²) dμ = ofReal((2s + L)²)·μ(B̄_r(ξ)). ∎
proof_key_steps: q(v) := v − p_S(v) is additive and |q(v)| ≤ |v|, because q = p_{S⊥}.
For x ∈ spt μ ∩ B̄_r(ξ), pick y ∈ F within s and split x − ξ = (x − y) + (y − x₀) + (x₀ − ξ) to get |q(x − ξ)| ≤ s + L + s.
spt μ has full μ-measure, so the bound holds μ⌞B̄_r(ξ)-a.e.; integrating gives ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} |q(x − ξ)|² dμ ≤ (2s + L)²·μ(B̄_r(ξ)).

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean type agree. The complementary orthogonal projection is additive and contractive, so the three-term decomposition gives 2s + L. Support is conull for any measure on finite-dimensional Euclidean space. The pointwise bound supplies the nonnegativity needed for squaring wherever used, and lower-integral monotonicity proves the stated L² estimate. The proof is complete and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Chebyshev selection of a point with small heights over a finite family (Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5, (1), (4), (5))
subproblem.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let μ be a measure on ℝ^P. Let T be a map from ℝ^P to linear subspaces of ℝ^P such that x ↦ p_{T(x)} is μ-a.e. strongly measurable; here p_{T(x)} is the orthogonal projection onto T(x), viewed as a continuous linear endomorphism of ℝ^P (Lean (T x).starProjection). Let Q be a property of points of ℝ^P that holds for μ-a.e. x, F ⊆ ℝ^P a finite set, ξ ∈ ℝ^P, and r, s, c, λ real numbers with r > 0 and s ≤ r.
Conventions: B̄_t(y) is the closed ball; ofReal = ENNReal.ofReal; integrals of [0, ∞]-valued functions are lower Lebesgue integrals; the quotient below is 0 at x = y (Lean's convention a/0 = 0); #F is the cardinality of F.
Suppose:
(i) dist(y, ξ) ≤ r for every y ∈ F;
(ii) for every y ∈ F, ∫_{B̄_{2r}(y)} ofReal(|(x − y) − p_{T(x)}(x − y)|² / |x − y|^m) dμ(x) ≤ ofReal(c);
(iii) (#F)·ofReal((2r)^m·c) < ofReal(λ)·μ(B̄_s(ξ)) in [0, ∞].
Then there is x₀ ∈ B̄_s(ξ) with Q(x₀) such that |(y − x₀) − p_{T(x₀)}(y − x₀)|² ≤ λ for every y ∈ F.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (T : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (Q : Euclid P → Prop) (F : Finset (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P) (r s c lam : ℝ), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x => (T x).starProjection) μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, Q x) → 0 < r → s ≤ r → (∀ y ∈ F, dist y ξ ≤ r) → (∀ y ∈ F, ∫⁻ x in closedBall y (2 * r), ENNReal.ofReal (‖(x - y) - (T x).starProjection (x - y)‖ ^ 2 / ‖x - y‖ ^ m) ∂μ ≤ ENNReal.ofReal c) → (F.card : ℝ≥0∞) * ENNReal.ofReal ((2 * r) ^ m * c) < ENNReal.ofReal lam * μ (closedBall ξ s) → ∃ x₀ ∈ closedBall ξ s, Q x₀ ∧ ∀ y ∈ F, ‖(y - x₀) - (T x₀).starProjection (y - x₀)‖ ^ 2 ≤ lam
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Steps 3–5 and the first inequality of Step 6 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5 (book chapter-05.txt lines 309–358): the estimate (1) on B_2(y), the summation over j, Chebyshev's inequality (4) and the choice (5) of x₀. Here it is stated for an arbitrary measure μ and subspace field T, with the a.e. property Q, the integral bounds (ii) and the mass condition (iii) as hypotheses.
Notation:
- For a subspace S and v ∈ ℝ^P, q_S(v) := v − p_S(v); q_S is linear because p_S is.
- For y ∈ F and x ∈ ℝ^P, f_y(x) := ofReal(|q_{T(x)}(x − y)|²) ∈ [0, ∞), and Ψ(x) := Σ_{y∈F} f_y(x).
- For a set E, ∫_E g dμ is the lower Lebesgue integral of g against μ⌞E.
- Closed balls are Borel sets, so μ⌞B̄_t(y)-a.e. point lies in B̄_t(y) (ae_restrict_mem).

1. Measurability. Fix y ∈ F; the map x ↦ x − y is continuous. Apply the continuous bilinear evaluation map (L, v) ↦ L v to the μ-a.e. strongly measurable x ↦ p_{T(x)} and the continuous x ↦ x − y. This shows x ↦ p_{T(x)}(x − y) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂, applied to the identity map of the space of continuous linear endomorphisms). Hence x ↦ q_{T(x)}(x − y), its norm and the square of its norm are μ-a.e. strongly measurable. So f_y is μ-a.e. measurable (AEMeasurable.ennreal_ofReal), also for every restriction of μ to a set.

2. Pointwise comparison (Simon (1)). Let y ∈ F and x ∈ B̄_{2r}(y), so |x − y| ≤ 2r. Put A := |q_{T(x)}(x − y)|² ≥ 0.
- If x = y, then x − y = 0 and q_{T(x)}(0) = 0, so A = 0 and A ≤ (2r)^m·(A/|x − y|^m) holds as 0 ≤ 0.
- If x ≠ y, then |x − y|^m > 0 and |x − y|^m ≤ (2r)^m (powers are monotone on [0, ∞)). Since A/|x − y|^m ≥ 0, A = |x − y|^m·(A/|x − y|^m) ≤ (2r)^m·(A/|x − y|^m).
Since (2r)^m ≥ 0, ofReal((2r)^m·b) = ofReal((2r)^m)·ofReal(b) for every real b (ENNReal.ofReal_mul). Hence f_y(x) ≤ ofReal((2r)^m)·ofReal(A/|x − y|^m) for every x ∈ B̄_{2r}(y).

3. The integral of each f_y. Let y ∈ F. For x ∈ B̄_r(ξ), dist(x, y) ≤ dist(x, ξ) + dist(ξ, y) ≤ r + r = 2r by (i), so B̄_r(ξ) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(y). Combine four facts:
- monotonicity of the integral in the domain (lintegral_mono_set);
- Step 2 for μ⌞B̄_{2r}(y)-a.e. x (lintegral_mono_ae);
- a finite constant comes out of a lower integral (lintegral_const_mul', since ofReal((2r)^m) ≠ ∞);
- hypothesis (ii).
They give ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} f_y dμ ≤ ∫_{B̄_{2r}(y)} f_y dμ ≤ ofReal((2r)^m)·∫_{B̄_{2r}(y)} ofReal(|q_{T(x)}(x − y)|²/|x − y|^m) dμ(x) ≤ ofReal((2r)^m)·ofReal(c) = ofReal((2r)^m·c).

4. Summation. By Step 1 each f_y is a.e. measurable for μ⌞B̄_r(ξ), so the integral of the finite sum is the sum of the integrals (lintegral_finsetSum'). By Step 3, ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} Ψ dμ = Σ_{y∈F} ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} f_y dμ ≤ Σ_{y∈F} ofReal((2r)^m·c) = (#F)·ofReal((2r)^m·c).

5. Choice of x₀ (Simon (4)–(5)), by contradiction. Suppose that for every x ∈ B̄_s(ξ) with Q(x) there is y ∈ F with |q_{T(x)}(y − x)|² > λ.
(a) Lower bound at such x. By linearity q_{T(x)}(x − y) = −q_{T(x)}(y − x), so |q_{T(x)}(x − y)| = |q_{T(x)}(y − x)|. Hence f_y(x) = ofReal(|q_{T(x)}(y − x)|²) ≥ ofReal(λ) (ofReal is monotone), and Ψ(x) ≥ f_y(x) ≥ ofReal(λ) because every summand of Ψ is ≥ 0 (Finset.single_le_sum).
(b) This holds μ⌞B̄_s(ξ)-a.e. Q holds μ-a.e., hence μ⌞B̄_s(ξ)-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae), and μ⌞B̄_s(ξ)-a.e. point lies in B̄_s(ξ). So Ψ ≥ ofReal(λ) holds μ⌞B̄_s(ξ)-a.e.
(c) Contradiction. Since s ≤ r, B̄_s(ξ) ⊆ B̄_r(ξ). By the integral of a constant over a set (setLIntegral_const), lintegral_mono_ae, lintegral_mono_set and Step 4,
ofReal(λ)·μ(B̄_s(ξ)) = ∫_{B̄_s(ξ)} ofReal(λ) dμ ≤ ∫_{B̄_s(ξ)} Ψ dμ ≤ ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} Ψ dμ ≤ (#F)·ofReal((2r)^m·c).
This contradicts (iii).

6. Conclusion. The supposition of Step 5 fails. Hence there is x₀ ∈ B̄_s(ξ) with Q(x₀) and |q_{T(x₀)}(y − x₀)|² ≤ λ, i.e. |(y − x₀) − p_{T(x₀)}(y − x₀)|² ≤ λ, for every y ∈ F. ∎
proof_key_steps: x ↦ |(x − y) − p_{T(x)}(x − y)|² is μ-a.e. measurable because x ↦ p_{T(x)} is a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂).
On B̄_{2r}(y), |q|² ≤ (2r)^m·|q|²/|x − y|^m; with B̄_r(ξ) ⊆ B̄_{2r}(y) and (ii) this gives ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} |q_{T(x)}(x − y)|² dμ ≤ (2r)^m c.
Summing over y ∈ F gives ∫_{B̄_r(ξ)} Ψ dμ ≤ #F·(2r)^m c, where Ψ(x) = Σ_y |q_{T(x)}(x − y)|².
If every Q-point x of B̄_s(ξ) had some |q_{T(x)}(y − x)|² > λ, then Ψ ≥ λ a.e. on B̄_s(ξ), so λ·μ(B̄_s(ξ)) ≤ #F·(2r)^m c, contradicting (iii).

subproblem.title: Finite maximal separated net from a lower ball-measure bound (Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5, (2)–(3))
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Lean: Measure (Euclid P), Borel σ-algebra), let K, A ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let s > 0 be real and a ∈ (0, ∞] (Lean ℝ≥0∞ with 0 < a). Suppose μ(A) < ∞, and for every y ∈ K the closed ball B̄_{s/2}(y) = {w : dist(w, y) ≤ s/2} is contained in A and satisfies a ≤ μ(B̄_{s/2}(y)). Then there is a finite set F ⊆ K (Lean: a Finset with ↑F ⊆ K) such that (#F)·a ≤ μ(A) in [0, ∞] and every x ∈ K satisfies dist(x, y) ≤ s for some y ∈ F.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (K A : Set (Euclid P)) (s : ℝ) (a : ℝ≥0∞), 0 < s → 0 < a → μ A ≠ ∞ → (∀ y ∈ K, closedBall y (s / 2) ⊆ A) → (∀ y ∈ K, a ≤ μ (closedBall y (s / 2))) → ∃ F : Finset (Euclid P), (↑F : Set (Euclid P)) ⊆ K ∧ (F.card : ℝ≥0∞) * a ≤ μ A ∧ ∀ x ∈ K, ∃ y ∈ F, dist x y ≤ s
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon Ch. 5, proof of Lemma 2.5 (book chapter-05.txt lines 316–334). That passage combines the 'general principle' that a maximal family of points y_j ∈ K with pairwise disjoint balls B_{σ/2}(y_j) satisfies K ⊆ ⋃_j B_σ(y_j), the counting estimate (3), and N ≤ Cδ^{−αn}. Here it is stated for an arbitrary measure, with the lower bound a and the container A as hypotheses.
Notation: B̄_t(y) := {w : dist(w, y) ≤ t}; #G is the cardinality of a finite set G. A finite set G ⊆ ℝ^P is s-separated if dist(y, y') > s for all distinct y, y' ∈ G. Arithmetic of measures is in [0, ∞].

1. Disjointness. Let G be s-separated and y ≠ y' in G. If w ∈ B̄_{s/2}(y) ∩ B̄_{s/2}(y'), then dist(y, y') ≤ dist(y, w) + dist(w, y') ≤ s/2 + s/2 = s, contradicting dist(y, y') > s. Hence the closed balls B̄_{s/2}(y), y ∈ G, are pairwise disjoint.

2. Counting bound. Let G ⊆ K be finite and s-separated. Closed balls are closed, hence Borel, sets. By Step 1 and finite additivity of μ (Mathlib measure_biUnion_finset), μ(⋃_{y∈G} B̄_{s/2}(y)) = Σ_{y∈G} μ(B̄_{s/2}(y)) ≥ Σ_{y∈G} a = (#G)·a, because a ≤ μ(B̄_{s/2}(y)) for y ∈ G ⊆ K. Every ball B̄_{s/2}(y) with y ∈ G ⊆ K lies in A, so by monotonicity (#G)·a ≤ μ(⋃_{y∈G} B̄_{s/2}(y)) ≤ μ(A).

3. Uniform bound on cardinalities. Since a ≠ 0 and μ(A) ≠ ∞, the Archimedean property of [0, ∞] (Mathlib ENNReal.exists_nat_mul_gt) gives N₀ ∈ ℕ with μ(A) < N₀·a. Every finite s-separated G ⊆ K then has #G < N₀. Otherwise N₀ ≤ #G, and Step 2 gives N₀·a ≤ (#G)·a ≤ μ(A) < N₀·a, which is absurd.

4. A separated family of maximal cardinality. The empty set is a finite s-separated subset of K of cardinality 0 ≤ N₀. Let m be the largest integer in {0, 1, …, N₀} that is the cardinality of some finite s-separated subset of K. It exists because 0 is such an integer (Mathlib Nat.findGreatest, Nat.findGreatest_spec). Choose a finite s-separated F ⊆ K with #F = m. By Step 2, (#F)·a ≤ μ(A).

5. Covering property. Let x ∈ K and suppose, for contradiction, that dist(x, y) > s for every y ∈ F.
(a) x ∉ F, because dist(x, x) = 0 < s.
(b) F' := F ∪ {x} is a finite subset of K, and it is s-separated. Two distinct points of F are more than s apart by the choice of F. For y ∈ F, dist(x, y) > s and dist(y, x) = dist(x, y) > s.
(c) #F' = m + 1. By Step 3, m + 1 < N₀, so m + 1 lies in {0, …, N₀} and is the cardinality of a finite s-separated subset of K.
(d) The maximality of m in Step 4 (Nat.le_findGreatest) gives m + 1 ≤ m, a contradiction.
Hence every x ∈ K satisfies dist(x, y) ≤ s for some y ∈ F.

6. Conclusion. F is a finite subset of K with (#F)·a ≤ μ(A) (Step 4) and the covering property of Step 5. ∎
proof_key_steps: For a finite s-separated G ⊆ K, the closed balls B̄_{s/2}(y), y ∈ G, are pairwise disjoint Borel subsets of A of measure ≥ a, so (#G)·a ≤ μ(A).
Since 0 < a and μ(A) < ∞ there is N₀ ∈ ℕ with μ(A) < N₀·a, so every such G has #G < N₀.
Take a finite s-separated F ⊆ K of maximal cardinality (Nat.findGreatest below N₀); then (#F)·a ≤ μ(A).
If some x ∈ K were more than s from every point of F, F ∪ {x} would be a larger s-separated subset of K; hence F is an s-net of K.

audit.reason: Prose and the standalone one-line Lean proposition match, including arbitrary K and A and the possibility a = ∞. Disjoint measurable balls give the counting bound; positive a and finite container measure bound all separated-family cardinalities. A maximum-cardinality family therefore covers K. The supplied proof is complete and needs no omitted compactness or measurability hypothesis.

subproblem.title: Approximate tangent planes of an integer multiplicity triple are n-dimensional μ_R-a.e.
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (Lean IMRep U n; M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult). Its weight is μ_R := R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ, where Hⁿ = μHE[n]. Then for μ_R-almost every x ∈ ℝ^P the subspace T_xM := approxTangentPlane n M x has dimension n: Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n. Here approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen approximate tangent plane of M at x when one exists, and the zero subspace otherwise.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x) = n
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the structural fact used in Step 5 of the parent proof: 'μ-a.e. x is a point where M has an n-dimensional approximate tangent plane T_xM = approxTangentPlane n M x'. It comes from IMRep.orients and the definition of approxTangentPlane (Simon Ch. 6, Definition 3.1; Ch. 3, Definition 1.4).
Notation: M := R.carrier, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, μ_R := R.measure.

1. The dimension is part of the tangent predicate. In SimonGMT Chapter03, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q is defined as the conjunction of Module.finrank ℝ Q = n with the blow-up convergence condition of Simon Ch. 3, 1.4. Its first component is the accessor HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq.

2. Pointwise consequence. Fix x such that some subspace Q satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q, and let h denote the statement ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q.
(a) In the frozen contract, approxTangentPlane n M x is the dependent if-then-else 'if h : ∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q then h.choose else ⊥'.
(b) Since h holds, approxTangentPlane n M x = h.choose (dite_eq_left, formerly dif_pos).
(c) h.choose satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x h.choose (Exists.choose_spec).
(d) By Step 1, Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n.

3. Existence ν-a.e. The field R.orients of the triple states: for ν-almost every x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (R.orient x) Q. Discarding the second conjunct, the property E(x) :≡ (∃ Q, HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q) holds for ν-a.e. x.

4. Transfer to μ_R. μ_R = ν.withDensity (x ↦ θ(x)) is absolutely continuous with respect to ν (Mathlib withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), so every ν-null set is μ_R-null. Applied to the ν-null set {x : ¬E(x)} (Measure.AbsolutelyContinuous.ae_le), this shows that E(x) holds for μ_R-a.e. x.

5. Conclusion. By Step 2, Module.finrank ℝ (approxTangentPlane n M x) = n at every x with E(x). By Step 4 this holds for μ_R-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q contains finrank Q = n as its first conjunct (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.finrank_eq).
If some approximate tangent space exists at x, approxTangentPlane n M x is the chosen one (dite_eq_left/dif_pos, Exists.choose_spec), so it has dimension n.
R.orients gives existence for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x; since R.measure = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, it holds R.measure-a.e.

audit.reason: The exact proposition follows directly from the pinned definitions. R.orients supplies approximate tangent existence almost everywhere for the restricted Hausdorff measure; absolute continuity transfers this to R.measure. The chosen tangent satisfies the predicate's dimension conjunct. The proof is complete, independent and valid for every stated P and n.
